title: Acute Kidney Injury: Urine Output, Creatinine and Reversible Causes
subject: Ward Protocols
preview: Acute kidney injury is a change in kidney function detected by creatinine trend or reduced urine output, interpreted with timing and context.
quickRevision: Acute kidney injury is a change in kidney function detected by creatinine trend or reduced urine output, interpreted with timing and context.
A normal creatinine early in injury may be misleading because serum creatinine can lag behind a fall in GFR.
Urinalysis, electrolytes and appropriate renal imaging help distinguish functional, intrinsic and obstructive causes.

sections.title: Recognize the situation
points: Acute kidney injury is a change in kidney function detected by creatinine trend or reduced urine output, interpreted with timing and context.
Evaluate volume status, shock, nephrotoxins, obstruction and underlying kidney disease; review medication doses.

sections.title: Clinical decisions & differential
points: A normal creatinine early in injury may be misleading because serum creatinine can lag behind a fall in GFR.
Urinalysis, electrolytes and appropriate renal imaging help distinguish functional, intrinsic and obstructive causes.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not assume all oliguria needs fluids; pulmonary edema and obstructive causes require different approaches.

quiz.question: Which cause of acute kidney injury is potentially reversible by relieving blockage?
quiz.explanation: Postrenal urinary obstruction. Evaluate volume status, shock, nephrotoxins, obstruction and underlying kidney disease; review medication doses.
